newsitem.title: USA: Lott sees hitch in Herman Cabinet nomination.
newsitem.headline: Lott sees hitch in Herman Cabinet nomination.

text.p: Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott said Monday that the Senate would not consider the nomination of Alexis Herman as Labor Secretary until President Clinton clarifies policy on requiring that federal construction contracts be performed by union labor.

"The intent had been to bring it (the nomination) up tomorrow. I have to get clearance from 99 senators to make that happen. Right now it doesn't look like that will happen," Lott told reporters. He said there were a number of objections from senators to going ahead with the nomination.
Lott said senators were concerned that the president might be trying to carry out by executive order regulations that should be subject to a congressional vote.
"We think it's a big mistake for the president to be suggesting that order to get federal contracts he must in fact meet the approval of labour unions," Lott said.

He said that the question of how Congress proceeded on funding the Labour Department and acting on the nominees for the department "is in doubt until we get some clarification about what their intentions are in that area."

In a speech to the AFL-CIO executive council in February Vice President Al Gore pledged White House support for labour unions. "The president and I stand on the side of working men and women who want to exercise their right to unionize, so we're going to send a message to companies that want to do business with the federal government - how you treat your employees and how you treat unions counts with us," Gore said.
